Subject: Trail tips for your next stretch of miles
CTA: Read more on the Northbay trail blog -> https://www.northbaysupply.com/blog/trail-tips
Body: Hey,

This is a game-changing season for us at Northbay Supply, and we're glad you're along for it.

But right now, let's talk about your trip.

A few trail tips we've been thinking about heading into this season:

**Pack weight adds up in the details.**
Before you leave the trailhead, weigh your loaded pack. Most day hikers are surprised to find they're carrying 8–12 lbs before food and water. Knowing your baseline helps you make smarter cuts on longer carries.

**Layer for the descent, not just the climb.**
You'll heat up on the way up — that part's easy to dress for. Plan your layers around what you'll need when you stop moving and the temperature drops. A stopped body cools faster than you expect.

**Know your water math.**
A general rule: 0.5 liters per hour of moderate hiking in mild conditions. Add heat, elevation gain, or pack weight and that number climbs. Don't rely on sources you haven't confirmed are accessible.

**Trekking poles aren't just for descents.**
They reduce stress on your knees going down, but on steep ascents they also help distribute load across your upper body — useful on long days above 8,000 ft.

**Tell someone your route. Every time.**
Not a tip you haven't heard. Worth repeating anyway.

More to come from us this season. We're building toward something and we'll share it with you as it's ready.

Get outside,
The Northbay Supply Team
